---
title: "Mutant Proteoform Prediction"
description: "Call somatic DNA and RNA variants from long-read DNA and RNA sequencing, link them, and translate the assembled transcripts to mutant proteoforms and peptides."
---

This pipeline is Exacto's primary use case: identify somatic DNA variants in a case sample (for
example a tumor) against a matched control, assemble the case's transcriptome from long RNA reads,
call RNA variants on them, link each RNA variant to the DNA variant that explains it, and translate
the transcripts to proteoforms whose every amino acid records the variants it came from.

External tools you'll need alongside Exacto:

- [`Minimap2`](https://github.com/lh3/minimap2) — long-read DNA and RNA alignment
- [`Samtools`](https://www.htslib.org/) — BAM sorting and indexing

## Step 1. Align the DNA reads

Align the tumor and normal long-read DNA to the reference genome, then sort and index. `--cs` is
required: Exacto reads variants from the `cs` tag.

```bash
# Tumor
minimap2 -ax map-hifi --cs --eqx -Y -L \
    reference_genome.fasta tumor_dna.fastq.gz \
    | samtools sort -o tumor_dna.sorted.bam
samtools index tumor_dna.sorted.bam

# Normal: repeat with normal_dna.fastq.gz -> normal_dna.sorted.bam
```

## Step 2. Call somatic DNA variants

Call the variants of the tumor that the normal does not carry. Use `--preset pb` for PacBio HiFi
reads or `--preset ont` for Oxford Nanopore reads:

```bash
exacto call-somatic-dna-vars \
    --bam-file tumor_dna.sorted.bam \
    --bai-file tumor_dna.sorted.bam.bai \
    --control-bam-files normal_dna.sorted.bam \
    --control-bai-files normal_dna.sorted.bam.bai \
    --fasta-file reference_genome.fasta \
    --preset pb \
    --output-tsv-file tumor_somatic_dna_variants.tsv
```

Germline variants are called the same way with
[`call-germline-dna-vars`](../cli/call-germline-dna-vars.qmd), from one BAM file.

## Step 3. Assemble the tumor transcriptome

Run the [Variant-aware Transcriptome Assembly](variant-aware-transcriptome-assembly.qmd) pipeline on the tumor's
long RNA reads, Steps 1 to 9: two passes of clustering with correction in between, one consensus
sequence per transcript, and reference stitching of degraded ends. This step uses the files:

- `pass2/tumor_pass2_exacto_rna_consensus.tsv` (the consensus sequences and their reads)
- `stitched/tumor_exacto_stitched_transcripts.tsv` (the stitched sequences)
- `stitched/tumor_exacto_stitched_transcripts.sorted.bam` (the stitched sequences, aligned)

## Step 4. Call RNA variants

```bash
exacto call-rna-transcript-vars \
    --bam-file stitched/tumor_exacto_stitched_transcripts.sorted.bam \
    --reference-genome-fasta-file reference_genome.fasta \
    --reference-gene-annotation-file gencode.gtf.gz \
    --reference-gene-annotation-source gencode \
    --reference-gene-annotation-assembly hg38 \
    --reference-gene-annotation-version v45 \
    --dna-variants-tsv-files tumor_somatic_dna_variants.tsv \
    --output-dir rna_variants/ \
    --output-prefix tumor
```

`--dna-variants-tsv-files` is optional: an RNA variant that matches a DNA variant (same chromosomes,
operations, type and sequence, each position within `--dna-variant-match-buffer` bases) gets that
variant's origin in the `origin` column.

## Step 5. Link RNA variants to DNA variants

```bash
exacto integrate-vars \
    --dna-variants-tsv-file tumor_somatic_dna_variants.tsv \
    --rna-variants-tsv-file rna_variants/tumor_exacto_assembled_transcript_variants.tsv \
    --reference-gene-annotation-file gencode.gtf.gz \
    --reference-gene-annotation-source gencode \
    --reference-gene-annotation-assembly hg38 \
    --reference-gene-annotation-version v45 \
    --output-tsv-file tumor_integrated_variants.tsv
```

`--dna-variants-tsv-file` also accepts a callset from another caller, written in the variant
grammar (see the [FAQ](../faq.qmd)).

## Step 6. Translate the transcripts to proteoforms

`translate-transcripts` takes the transcript sequences from the consensus TSV, replaced by the
stitched sequences when `--stitched-transcripts-tsv-file` is given. The `call-rna-transcript-vars`
tables must then come from the stitched alignment, as in Step 4:

```bash
exacto translate-transcripts \
    --assembled-transcript-model-alignments-tsv-file rna_variants/tumor_exacto_assembled_transcript_model_alignments.tsv \
    --assembled-transcript-variants-tsv-file rna_variants/tumor_exacto_assembled_transcript_variants.tsv \
    --dna-variants-tsv-file tumor_somatic_dna_variants.tsv \
    --integrated-variants-tsv-file tumor_integrated_variants.tsv \
    --rna-consensus-tsv-file pass2/tumor_pass2_exacto_rna_consensus.tsv \
    --stitched-transcripts-tsv-file stitched/tumor_exacto_stitched_transcripts.tsv \
    --strategy longest_orf \
    --output-dir translation/ \
    --output-prefix tumor
```

Transcripts assembled outside exacto are translated by passing
`--assembled-transcripts-support-tsv-file` instead of `--rna-consensus-tsv-file`.

## Step 7. Call mutant peptides

Cut each proteoform into peptides of 8 to 11 amino acids (`--min-k`, `--max-k`) and keep those that
overlap a mutant amino acid and do not occur in the reference proteome:

```bash
exacto call-peptide-vars \
    --proteoforms-tsv-file translation/tumor_exacto_proteoforms.tsv \
    --reference-fasta-file reference_proteome.fasta \
    --output-tsv-file tumor_peptide_variants.tsv \
    --output-fasta-file tumor_peptide_variants.fasta
```

::: {.callout-warning}
`call-peptide-vars` builds a k-mer index of the reference proteome, which takes about 16 GB of
memory for a human proteome. Budget for it when running several samples at once.
:::

## Outputs

| File | Produced by | Description |
|:-----|:------------|:------------|
| `tumor_somatic_dna_variants.tsv` | `call-somatic-dna-vars` | Somatic DNA variants |
| `rna_variants/tumor_exacto_assembled_transcript_variants.tsv` | `call-rna-transcript-vars` | RNA variants per transcript |
| `rna_variants/tumor_exacto_assembled_transcript_model_alignments.tsv` | `call-rna-transcript-vars` | Each transcript's structure against the genome |
| `tumor_integrated_variants.tsv` | `integrate-vars` | RNA variants linked to the DNA variants that explain them |
| `translation/tumor_exacto_proteoforms.tsv` | `translate-transcripts` | Proteoforms with their mutant amino acid intervals and source variants |
| `translation/tumor_exacto_proteoforms.fasta` | `translate-transcripts` | Proteoform sequences |
| `translation/tumor_exacto_proteoform_nucleotides.tsv` | `translate-transcripts` | Per-nucleotide provenance of each proteoform |
| `tumor_peptide_variants.tsv` | `call-peptide-vars` | Mutant peptides |
